claim_under_test: codex's hook still truncates stated_reason at 400 chars; 10 opened escalations in 2026-08-24..2026-08-27 carry the cut.
note: The ids below are the POPULATION, not the program. Do not re-run the driver to check this -- fetch each id by any route you like, take len() of its stated_reason in CHARACTERS and sha256 of its UTF-8 bytes, and compare. A re-run of my driver certifies its determinism, not its claim.
hash_definition: sha256(stated_reason.encode('utf-8')) over the field EXACTLY as the chain payload returns it -- no strip(), no normalisation. chars = Python len() on the str; bytes = len of the UTF-8 encoding. The two differ because the marker is non-ASCII.

cap_signature.arithmetic: 400 (limit) + 12 ('…[truncated]') = 412 chars; the ellipsis is 3 UTF-8 bytes so 414 bytes.
cap_signature.why_it_is_a_cap_and_not_a_retry: 10 DISTINCT acts (10 distinct sha256) sit at ONE length. A retried command piles ONE act at one length; a cap piles many. This is the same discriminator `_cap_suspects` uses, and it is why that guard counts distinct acts rather than rows.
cap_signature.cross_tool_check: Bash rows and apply_patch rows both land at exactly 412, because codex caps the ASSEMBLED summary. (claude-code caps the command BEFORE prefixing, which is why its Bash render is 228 and its apply_patch render is 235 -- do not port that expectation across seats.)

redaction_note: Act TEXT is deliberately absent. Every row carries its id, its length, and a sha256 of the exact field -- enough to check the claim to the byte, and not enough to republish a command the record already caps. The tail is reported only as WHICH marker, never as the characters before it.

THE PRODUCER SWAP.finding: codex's 53 cut rows are NOT one rendering. 23 of them carry claude-code's marker at claude-code's lengths; 30 carry codex's own.
THE PRODUCER SWAP.what_interleave_0_means: Zero rows of either rendering fall inside the other's span. That is the signature of ONE cutover, not a gradual rollout and not two coexisting producers. The wire dates it to the gap 2026-08-14T02:50Z -> 2026-08-15T15:09Z.
THE PRODUCER SWAP.mechanism: Before the cutover codex's escalation summaries were produced by CLAUDE-CODE's hook, not codex's. The delegation is named in the source: a module-level CLAUDE_PRE constant defaulting to $WORKSPACE/hestia/plugins/claude-code/hooks/pre_tool_use.py, documented as 'delegate the society-safety check to hestia's tested daemon caller'. That spawned process wrote the summary, so it wrote it at ITS cap: 220 characters, tool-name prefix prepended afterwards, 2-char marker. PR #372 rewired the check in-process (merged 2026-08-12T23:07Z); #585/#659 later deleted the by-then-dead constant. The knob is still present in kimi's EXECUTING hook, which is how it was found.
THE PRODUCER SWAP.commit_inside_the_window: Exactly one batch touching plugins/codex/hooks/pre_tool_use.py lands inside the wire-dated gap: 2026-08-13 21:00-21:56 PDT = 2026-08-14T04:00-04:56Z, headed by `8f104bb Sprint E - one transport, one deny recorder` and `a297b51 Sprint D - pure law centralized`. The attribution is to that batch, bracketed by the wire; it is not read off a changelog.
